name: Wild Herbs
description: Bright, green, aromatic

name: Wild Berries
description: Sweet-tart burst, jammy

name: Black Fig
description: Dried in goatskin sacks for months. Jammy, almost wine-like. Older than agriculture itself.

name: Chamomile
description: Gentle, calming floral

name: Citrus Peel
description: Zesty, bitter oils

name: Galangal
description: Ginger's harder, denser cousin — piney, citrusy, medicinal. Used in jamu tonics for over 1,300 years.

name: Hibiscus
description: Jamaica / Bissap / Karkadé — one flower, four continents, one ruby-red sour tradition.

name: Kaffir Lime Leaf
description: Double-lobed leaves so fragrant a single torn leaf scents a room. Essential to Thai and Indonesian cooking.

name: Medjool Date
description: The king of dates — reserved for Moroccan royalty. Concentrated sweetness with iron depth.

name: Palm Sugar
description: Gula Jawa — boiled palm sap with terroir. Tastes of caramel, smoke, and toffee. Made in Java 1,000+ years.

name: Pandan
description: The vanilla of Southeast Asia — green, grassy, impossibly fragrant. Dyes anything a vivid jade.

name: Piloncillo
description: Unrefined dark cane sugar in cone form. Smells of tropical smoke and fermented cane. Ancestor of brown sugar.

name: Tamarind
description: The 'Indian date' that grew in Africa, named in Arabic, and now anchors cuisines across five continents.

name: Fresh Turmeric
description: The golden root that stains everything. 4,000 years of cultivation. Every jamu begins here.

name: Achiote
description: Annatto seeds so orange they were used as war paint. Cheddar gets its color from this. Mild and earthy.

name: Amazake
description: Sweet sake without alcohol. Drunk by samurai before battle. Called 'drinkable IV drip' for its nutrition.

name: Borage Flower
description: Sky-blue star-shaped flowers that taste of cool cucumber. Herbalists called it 'the herb of courage.'

name: Cacao Nibs
description: Aztec cacao beans were currency. The xocolatl drink — cold, bitter, chili-spiced — is 4,000 years old.

name: Cassis
description: Blackcurrant — banned in the US for 50 years. Deep purple, intensely tart, the soul of Burgundy's Kir.

name: Epazote
description: Smells aggressively of turpentine and citrus — dangerous in large doses. Indispensable in small ones.

name: Ginger Root
description: Sharp warm heat that builds

name: Harissa Pepper
description: Tunisia's national condiment — stone-pounded by hand before dawn. Every family's recipe fiercer than the last.

name: Hojicha
description: A 1920s Kyoto tea merchant roasted unsellable leaves in desperation. Panic led to something beautiful.

name: Laksa Leaf
description: Vietnamese mint — not true mint but mint-intense with a peppery, pungent edge. Essential to laksa.

name: Lavender
description: Provence lavender harvested since Roman times. Too much tastes of soap. Used correctly — purple fragrance.

name: Orange Blossom Water
description: Distilled from bitter orange blossoms — a single teaspoon perfumes an entire dish.

name: Pink Peppercorn
description: Not a true pepper — the dried berry of a Peruvian tree. Fruity, mild, resinous. French chefs adore it.

name: Preserved Lemon
description: Whole lemons packed in salt for weeks — bitterness dissolves into something sour and ancient.

name: Quince
description: The golden apple of mythology — inedible raw, magical cooked. Turns rose-pink during fermentation.

name: Roasted Acorn
description: Nutty, smoky, surprisingly sweet

name: Rooibos
description: Khoisan people's Cederberg mountain tea — caffeine-free, naturally sweet, a remedy for centuries.

name: Rose Water
description: Harvested at dawn before essential oils evaporate. Every drop holds two weeks of blooming season.

name: Shiso
description: Green: basil, mint, anise at once. Red: sharp and medicinal. Contains natural antimicrobial compounds.

name: Sour Cherry
description: Tart, deep red, complex

name: Sumac
description: The lemon of the ancient world. Used by Romans and Phoenicians before citrus reached the Mediterranean.

name: Ume Plum
description: Closer to apricot than plum. Preserved as umeboshi or fermented into umeshu. Its acidity kills summer bacteria.

name: Verjus
description: Juice of unripe grapes — used since medieval France. Fresher than vinegar, wilder than wine.

name: Verveine
description: Lemon verbena from Argentina, adopted by French herbalists. Smells of lemon more intensely than lemon itself.

name: Wild Mushroom
description: Deep umami, forest floor

name: Za'atar
description: Wild herb blend with toasted sesame and sumac. Medieval physicians prescribed it to ward off evil spirits.

name: Aleppo Pepper
description: From ancient Aleppo — only 10,000 Scoville but oily and fruity with a slow-building warmth.

name: Argan Oil
description: Pressed from kernels of argan trees in Morocco's Souss Valley. Goats genuinely climb them.

name: Baobab Fruit
description: From trees that live 3,000 years. Tart as tamarind, creamy, with 6x the vitamin C of oranges.

name: Bergamot
description: From Calabria's sole growing region. Defines Earl Grey tea, Acqua di Cologne, and half the world's perfumes.

name: Black Lime
description: Whole limes boiled in brine then sun-dried to black. Inside: profoundly sour, slightly smoky, strangely savory.

name: Butterfly Pea Flower
description: Steeps indigo-blue. Add acid and watch it shift purple, then pink. A living pH indicator. Pure alchemy.

name: Cinnamon Bark
description: Warm, sweet, woody

name: Elderflower
description: Perfumy, delicate, ethereal

name: Gentian Root
description: The most bitter compound in nature — detectable at one part per 58 million. Primary bitter in Angostura.

name: Grains of Paradise
description: West African pepper worth more than black pepper in medieval Europe. Cardamom-warmth with citrus finish.

name: Juniper Berry
description: Piney, gin-forward, crisp

name: Koji
description: The mold that built Japanese civilization. Behind sake, miso, soy sauce. Japan's official national fungus.

name: Long Pepper
description: Slow-building heat that evolves

name: Mahlab
description: Ground cherry stones that smell of almonds and cherries simultaneously. One of the stranger beauties.

name: Matcha
description: Shade-grown leaves ground to powder. The shading forces more chlorophyll and L-theanine — calm alertness.

name: Mirabelle Plum
description: Golden plum of Lorraine, protected by French law. Only 3-4 weeks of harvest per year.

name: Ras el Hanout
description: The head of the shop — the very best a spice merchant has to offer. Up to thirty spices, no two blends alike.

name: Sakura Blossom
description: Cherry blossoms preserved in salt for months. A brew made with sakura tastes of spring — fleeting and gone.

name: Sanshō Pepper
description: From the prickly ash tree — creates tingling numbness as if small electric sparks dance across your lips.

name: Sea Buckthorn
description: So sour birds avoid it until frost. 15x more vitamin C than oranges. Stains everything vivid orange.

name: Szechuan Peppercorn
description: Creates mouth-numbing má — lemon zest, green flower, and static electricity. US import banned for 37 years.

name: Torch Ginger
description: Kecombrang — pink torch-shaped flower from Indonesian rainforest. Ginger heat, floral tartness, tropical scent.

name: Vanilla Pod
description: Rich, creamy, round

name: Wasabi Root
description: Real wasabi requires pristine mountain streams and 3 years to grow. Its heat hits the nose, not the tongue.

name: Wattleseed
description: Aboriginal Australians have eaten it for 6,000 years — roasted it tastes of coffee and chocolate simultaneously.

name: Yuzu
description: Japan's mountain citrus — mandarin, grapefruit, and something entirely its own. Export ban still in place.

name: Charcoal
description: Turns drinks jet black

name: Kabosu
description: The gentlest Japanese citrus — softer than sudachi, faintly bergamot-like. Brought by a Buddhist monk.

name: Kuromoji
description: Japanese spicebush with bark that smells of cinnamon and clove. Almost entirely unknown outside Japan.

name: Lemongrass
description: Bright, citrusy, Southeast Asian

name: Mastic
description: Crystallized resin from Chios trees, scored and harvested as teardrops. Alexander the Great chewed it.

name: Mezcal Worm Salt
description: Dried agave larvae ground with salt and chili. Pre-Columbian Oaxacan condiment that shocks first-timers.

name: Saffron Thread
description: Worth-its-weight golden luxury

name: Sudachi
description: Tiny green citrus from Tokushima, harvested before it ripens. Crisper and more mineral than lemon.

name: Tonka Bean
description: Almond + cherry + tobacco (banned IRL!)

name: Truffle Honey
description: Funky, luxurious, polarizing

name: Ancient Yeast
description: Thousands of years old. Transforms anything.

name: Chartreuse Herb Blend
description: Only two monks know the complete formula: 130 Alpine herbs. Glows green under UV light.

name: Dragon Pepper
description: Almost alive with heat. Handle with care.

name: The Dreaming Spore
description: Found on mushrooms that grow only on lightning-struck oaks. Turns brews unpredictable, chaotic, beautiful.

name: Ember Spice
description: Crystalline formations found in cooled lava flows. A single shard transforms a brew — it glows from within.

name: Glacial Memory
description: Ice from a glacier so ancient it contains prehistoric air bubbles. The brew tastes of before humanity.

name: Leviathan Salt
description: From ocean trenches where no light has ever reached. Crystallizes in deep indigo-blue. Adds abyssal weight.

name: Moonberry
description: Glows faint blue. Otherworldly.

name: Moonpetal Bloom
description: Grows only in moonlit clearings on the first night of the full moon, wilts at dawn. Brews that glow silver.

name: Phoenix Honey
description: Collected from volcanic beehives.

name: Phoenix Petal Ash
description: Ash gathered from a phoenix's still-warm rebirth nest. Transforms ruined brews into triumph.

name: Starfall Honey
description: Found in crystallized form after meteor showers. Iridescent — shifts gold, silver, and pale blue when stirred.

name: Starfruit
description: Cosmic sweetness from another realm

name: Worldroot Extract
description: From a root predating recorded history, found in amber soil. Contains the memory of every plant ever lived.
